subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 1: The Ever-Evolving World of Science
central_question: How does curiosity, questioning, observation and experimentation help science keep growing while connecting ideas about nature, society and responsibility?
in_scope_units: Opening invitation to science: science as exploration of the small and large, near and far, through questions, experiments and personal discovery.
Science as a process: asking how and why, recognising patterns, staying open to the unknown and learning through direct experience.
Science, society and responsibility: connecting human activity with the natural world, environmental challenges and sustainability.

Interconnected fields of science: links among physics, chemistry, biology and earth science and the Grade 7 journey through materials, electricity, changes, heat, water, life processes, time, light and space.
1.1 Happy Exploring!: Activity 1.1 Question the Answer, which develops creative scientific questioning from given answers.
banned_topics: Detailed acid-base classification, which belongs to Chapter 2.
Construction and analysis of electrical circuits, which belongs to Chapter 3.
Detailed properties of metals and non-metals, which belong to Chapter 4.
Formal classification of physical and chemical changes, which belongs to Chapter 5.
Detailed explanations of eclipses, planetary motion, circulation, photosynthesis or heat transfer, which are only previewed here.

known_pitfalls.claim: Science is mainly a collection of fixed facts to memorise.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter presents science as an ongoing process of asking questions, observing, experimenting and revising understanding.

known_pitfalls.claim: Only questions with one correct answer are useful in science.
known_pitfalls.correction: Activity 1.1 encourages many creative questions that may lead to the same answer and values interesting questioning.

known_pitfalls.claim: Physics, chemistry, biology and earth science are completely separate.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter explains that scientific fields are interconnected and ideas in one area often inspire questions in another.

known_pitfalls.claim: Experiments are useful only when they confirm what we expected.
known_pitfalls.correction: Even an experiment that confirms a prediction can raise new questions requiring more observations and experiments.

known_pitfalls.claim: Science is only about discovery and has nothing to do with society.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter connects science with responsibility, environmental challenges and creating a more sustainable world.

recommended_example_progression: Use the opening paper-plane discussion to connect simple observation with scientific exploration of flight.
Use the chapter overview of materials, electricity, changes, heat, water and life processes to show links among branches of science.
Use the light, shadow, day-night and eclipse preview to distinguish asking questions from teaching the later chapter details.
Use Activity 1.1 Question the Answer with 'Just add some milk' to model generating more than one reasonable question.
Use the Activity 1.1 answer '42' to discuss why an interesting question is better than an obvious arithmetic question.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: This introductory chapter has no separate end-of-chapter exercise section; its main structured task is Activity 1.1, 'Question the Answer'.
